visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) Two hands pull apart a freshly baked, golden-brown square of milk toast on a wire rack, revealing a steaming, white, and fibrous interior in a brightly lit kitchen studio. Subsequently, ingredients including flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, and water are poured into a clear glass bowl while a tiny animated woman figure drops into the frame via a small parachute. (2) A wooden spoon stirs the mixture into a shaggy dough as the tiny animated woman plays in the flour mounds. Real hands knead the dough on a floured countertop until it reaches a smooth consistency, eventually stretching a small portion of it to demonstrate the translucent 'windowpane' effect before placing it in a bowl to ferment. (3) A white, heavy square cast iron bread mold embossed with the 'Vermicular' brand logo is introduced on a wooden board. Hands use a wooden rolling pin to flatten the fermented dough pieces into long strips, then fold and roll them into tight spirals, with the tiny animated woman helper appearing to push the dough along. (4) The rolled dough pieces are placed side-by-side in the white mold for a second fermentation; the lid is slid closed and the mold is placed into a modern home oven. Finally, hands wearing striped blue and white oven mitts remove a perfect golden-brown bread cube from the mold and pull it apart to demonstrate its soft, cotton-like texture.

The background music is an upbeat acoustic guitar track featuring light pizzicato strings and a gentle, rhythmic percussion beat. The overall sound environment is pristine, indicating a professional studio recording with high clarity and no unwanted ambient noise. (2) The narration is punctuated by high-pitched, cartoonish 'ya-ya-ya' vocal effects followed by a synthesized explosion sound effect, which occurs as ingredients are mixed. A cheerful female cheer of 'Ye!' is heard briefly over the continuing background music and descriptive narration. (3) The narrator's pitch remains steady while describing the dough-shaping process, accompanied by soft percussive thuds as the dough is manipulated. A clear metallic clinking sound is heard when the heavy cast iron bread mold is handled, with the narrator explicitly articulating the brand name 'Vermicular'.
